scope: Read-only audit of this batch's stored browser oracle and relevant request/query source; no browser, tunnel, fixture, or service action.

corrected_claim.prior_progress_claim: Each of the five Dashboard APIs had four network failures while the loopback forward was stopped.
corrected_claim.reviewed_conclusion: The captured evidence does not directly prove application fetch rejection. It shows PerformanceResourceTiming entries with responseStatus=null and transferSize/encodedBodySize=0, plus listener count zero. Record these as unknown/zero-byte timing entries while the listener was absent; app rejection remains unverified.
corrected_claim.error_state_retry: Saved in-page observations show route `/`, main mounted, navigator.onLine=true, and no role=alert / Retry feedback. No user Retry click occurred. Record this as a needs-verification observation, not a product FAIL.

captured_urls.basis: The recorder added an API path only when URL origin equaled location.origin; it persisted only pathname, not the full URL or an initiator.

oracle_audit.performance_timing_limit: Null responseStatus and zero encoded/transfer sizes do not independently establish a rejected fetch.
oracle_audit.record_consistency: fault-observation.json (captured before forward restore) aggregates 4 unknown and 5 HTTP-200 timing entries per API; fault-result.json (captured after restore) contains a different cumulative timing aggregate. These recorder outputs are not reliable per-request failure oracles and do not carry absolute per-request timestamps.

fault_window.note: Persisted performance entries have monotonic start values but did not preserve performance.timeOrigin or per-event wall-clock timestamps.

source_oracles.fact: API base is /api. authenticatedFetch awaits window.fetch without a catch; requestWithResponse throws ApiError only after an HTTP response with !ok. A fetch rejection would propagate, but no rejection was persisted.
Dashboard loadDashboard uses Promise.all for five GET APIs.
ErrorState is rendered when query.isError or data is absent; its Retry button calls query.refetch.
QueryClient retry callback disables retries in DEV; production stops after failureCount > 3, while no retryDelay is configured in this source.
